title: Distillation and Small Models
summary: A small student model can learn from a large teacher's full output distribution, not just its final answers. This lesson covers soft targets and temperature, the distillation loss as a scaled KL divergence, the two ways LLM teams distil (logits and generated data), what it costs, and how it fits with pruning and the over-training strategy.
objectives: Explain why a teacher's soft probabilities carry more information than a hard label
Compute temperature-softened distributions and the T²-scaled KL distillation loss for a small example
Combine the distillation loss with the hard-label loss and say what each term does
Distinguish logit distillation from sequence-level (synthetic data) distillation and estimate the compute and storage of each
State the practical and licensing limits of distilling from another model and how to evaluate the student
prerequisites: You should know softmax and temperature ([Next-Token Prediction and Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling)), cross-entropy ([How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn)) and the SFT setup ([Instruction Tuning](/learn/training-and-adaptation/instruction-tuning)). KL divergence is defined here from scratch.
